metaDescription: Seven upholstery cleaners compared across portable machines and spot sprays, on heat, suction, tools, fabric codes and residue, with honest ownership notes.
expertTake: The Bissell Little Green HydroSteam is the best overall pick because it pairs heated water, three cleaning modes and a small tank that is easy to carry to a sofa. The Folex instant spot remover is the value pick for fresh spills on colorfast fabric. Skip machines and sprays entirely on velvet, suede and leather unless the label says it is safe, because those fabrics water-mark or lose finish.
introParagraphs: An upholstery cleaner is either a spray or foam that you apply and blot, or a small machine that sprays solution and sucks the dirty water back out. Sprays are cheap and fast for fresh spills, while machines pull dirt out of the cushion and suit older stains.

The most important choice is not the product but the fabric. Check the cleaning code tag first, test a hidden spot, and avoid over-wetting. A good cleaner on the wrong fabric leaves a ring or a stiff patch that is harder to fix than the original stain.

products.name: Bissell Little Green HydroSteam Portable Spot Cleaner 3618
products.description:
Bissell's Little Green HydroSteam combines hot water and steam with suction and an oxy formula, and it has three cleaning modes: SteamWash for tough, oily messes, Steam for refreshing upholstery and cleaning tile and grout, and Wash for everyday jobs.

A small extractor is the right scale for a sofa, because you can work on one cushion at a time and keep the fabric from soaking. Heated water helps loosen greasy and set-in stains, though a small onboard heater is not the same as a commercial steam clean. Compared with the Max Pet model, this one leans on heat rather than a dedicated pet tool. The three modes are the main reason it suits more than just sofas, since the steam mode also refreshes tile and grout.

Rinse both tanks after each job and let the parts air dry to prevent a sour smell. Clear the nozzle and screen, since clogs are the usual failure. Work from the outside edge of a stain toward the center so the stain does not spread, and make the final pass with clean water to lift remaining soap. Prop cushions on edge so air reaches both sides as they dry.
products.bestFor: Households that want a heated portable extractor for sofas and stairs.
pros: Hot water and steam help loosen greasy, set-in stains
Three modes cover washing, steaming and refreshing
Small size handles one cushion or stair at a time
Oxy formula works with the machine for stains
cons: Small tank means frequent refills on a large sofa
Highest price tier among the seven products

products.description:
The Max Pet version of the Little Green adds a self-cleaning tough stain tool and a pet hair removal tool, and it is meant to be used with a pet oxy spot and stain formula that includes a urine eliminator.

A self-cleaning tool rinses itself, which cuts down on residue and the sour smell that follows pet cleanups. The maker claims stronger suction than a competing portable, though there is no common standard for comparing suction figures between brands. Compared with the HydroSteam, it is built around pets rather than heat. The pet hair tool is useful on upholstery where hair sticks to fabric.

Treat old pet urine with an enzyme product first, and rinse both tanks after each use. After an accident, blot the liquid first and then use the machine, because pouring a lot of solution into a soaked cushion pushes urine deeper. Run clean water through the hose at the end to flush the lines.
products.bestFor: Pet owners who clean accidents off sofas and stairs.
pros: Self-cleaning tough stain tool reduces residue
Pet hair tool lifts hair from fabric
Pet formula includes a urine eliminator
Compact machine suits sofas and stairs
cons: No heating feature like the HydroSteam
Tank capacity is small for large jobs

products.name: Shark StainStriker Portable Carpet and Upholstery Cleaner PX202BRN
products.description:
Shark's StainStriker is a portable carpet and upholstery cleaner that mixes its stain-removing formula as you use it rather than relying on a premixed liquid that can lose strength over time, and it ships with four specialized tools.

Multiple tools matter on a sofa because a wide tool suits flat cushions while a small tool suits seams and stairs. The mixing approach is a maker claim about freshness, not a guarantee of results. Compared with the Uwant, it is a more conventional design with a brand-name solution. A kit of tools matters more than a headline figure when you clean seams and stairs.

Pick the right tool for each surface, rinse the tanks and let the unit dry before storing. Keep the small tools with the machine in a bag, since the crevice tool is the one people lose and the one you need on stairs. Empty the dirty tank outdoors if the water is very dark.
products.bestFor: Homes that want a range of tools for sofas, stairs and car seats.
pros: Four tools cover cushions, seams and stairs
Formula is mixed on use rather than premixed
Handles upholstery, carpet and area rugs
Portable size is easy to carry to a sofa
cons: Needs the maker's formula for best results
Higher price tier than a spray

products.name: MUJERBAY UltraHeat Portable Spot and Stain Cleaner
products.description:
MUJERBAY's UltraHeat machine heats cleaning solution to 140 degrees F in under 15 seconds to loosen tough stains, and it has universal wheels and a handle for easy moving. The maker says it cleans localized stains and conserves water.

140 degrees F is warm, not boiling, and quick heating helps because many small machines make you wait or rely on hot tap water. Wheels help on carpet but are less useful on a sofa. Compared with the Bissell HydroSteam, the heat claim is a number, and the HydroSteam has steam modes. Fast heating also means less waiting, which makes quick jobs more likely to get done.

Rinse the tanks, dry the parts and test the heat on a hidden spot first. A heated machine can set some protein stains if the water is too hot, so treat blood and milk with cold water first. Test on a hidden seam before you use the heat on a delicate fabric.
products.bestFor: Stains on carpet and sofas where a quick-heating machine saves time.
pros: Heats solution to 140 degrees F in under 15 seconds
Wheels and handle make it easy to move
Localized cleaning conserves water
Stated heat figure is checkable
cons: Wheels help on carpet more than on a sofa
Heat may be too much for delicate fabrics

products.name: Uwant 18Kpa Portable Cleaner with Pet Solution and 3 Brush Heads
products.description:
Uwant's portable cleaner is rated at 18 Kpa suction and comes with three brush heads and a pet-specific cleaning solution. It sprays, scrubs and suctions for furniture, car interiors and pet messes.

Suction figures have no common standard, so 18 Kpa is a rough guide rather than a proof of performance. Three brush heads give you options for fabric and carpet. Compared with the Shark, the solution is a pet formula and the brush heads are the main accessory. The three brush heads let you choose a gentler brush for fabric.

Rinse the tanks after use and clear the brush heads of hair. Pull hair from the brush heads after every job, because tangled hair reduces scrubbing. Replace the pet solution with a mild one if a fabric reacts to the fragrance.
products.bestFor: Pet households that want a suction-rated extractor with brush options.
pros: 18 Kpa suction rating gives a stated figure to compare
Three brush heads suit fabric and carpet
Pet-specific solution is included
Spray, scrub and suction in one machine
cons: Suction ratings are not comparable between brands
Brush heads collect hair and need cleaning

products.name: Folex Instant Carpet Spot Remover Spray, 32 oz

specList.label: Formula
specList.value: No VOCs, CFCs or petroleum, per the maker

products.description:
Folex is a spray spot remover in a 32 oz bottle. The maker says it works on upholstery, carpets and rugs that are colorfast and water-safe, needs no rinsing, and contains no VOCs, CFCs or petroleum.

A spray is the fastest tool for a fresh spill, because you apply it and blot immediately. No-rinse formulas leave less residue, but they work best on fresh stains and may need repeating on old ones. Compared with the Bissell machines, it is far cheaper but cannot extract deep dirt. It is also the cheapest option per spill in this lineup.

Test on a hidden spot, blot rather than rub and let the fabric dry fully. Spray lightly and blot with a clean white cloth, working from the edge inward, and avoid rubbing which can fuzz the fabric. Store the bottle upright and away from heat.
products.bestFor: Fresh spills on colorfast sofas and rugs.
pros: No rinsing needed, so less residue is left behind
32 oz bottle covers many spills at a lower tier
Maker states no VOCs, CFCs or petroleum
Works on upholstery, carpet and rugs
cons: Old, set-in stains may need repeated treatment
Not for delicate or non-colorfast fabrics

products.name: Carbona Oxy Powered Upholstery Cleaner with Brush and Sponge
products.description:
Carbona's cleaner is a 13.5 oz oxy powered spray with a built-in sponge and brush applicator. The sponge treats the stain and the brush loosens dirt, and the maker says it can be used on couches, mattresses and car seats.

An applicator head means you do not need a separate scrubber, though a brush can be too stiff for delicate fabrics. Oxygen-based cleaners work well on organic stains but can lighten some dyes. Compared with Folex, the smaller bottle and applicator suit a car or a single sofa. It is best kept as a small-job cleaner, not a whole-sofa solution.

Spot test first, brush gently and blot dry. Because the applicator head is built in, wipe the sponge clean after each use so it does not harden. For a mattress or a car seat, treat small sections and let each dry before moving on.
products.bestFor: Occasional spot cleaning of couches and car seats.
pros: Sponge and brush applicator handles scrubbing
13.5 oz size is handy for small jobs
Oxy formula targets organic stains
Works on couches, mattresses and car seats
cons: Brush head can be too stiff for delicate fabric
Oxy cleaners can lighten some dyes

buyingCriteria.explanation: Upholstery tags carry a code: W means water-based cleaners are safe, S means solvent only, WS means either and X means vacuum only. Most machines and sprays are water-based, so they suit W and WS fabrics. Check the tag before you buy, because the wrong cleaner can ruin a cushion. If the tag is missing, test a hidden spot with a dab of cleaner and wait for it to dry.

A spray like the Folex is fast and cheap for fresh spills. A machine like the Bissell HydroSteam pulls dirty water out of the cushion, which suits older stains. If you have pets or kids, a small extractor pays for itself, and if you have an occasional spill, a spray is enough. A machine also freshens a sofa that smells, which a spray does not.

The MUJERBAY heats to 140 degrees F in under 15 seconds, while the Bissell uses hot water and steam. Suction ratings like the Uwant's 18 Kpa have no common standard. Heat helps with grease, and suction decides how dry the cushion ends up. Heat can set some protein stains, so use cold water on blood and milk first.

The Shark includes four tools, and the Uwant adds three brush heads. Small tanks mean frequent refills on a big sofa. A flexible hose of about 4 to 5 ft is workable for stairs. Keep the tools together in a bag so nothing goes missing.

Avoid machines and harsh sprays on leather, velvet and suede unless the label allows it. Microfiber can water-mark, so use a minimal amount. Always test a hidden spot first. If you are unsure, ask the sofa maker for a care guide.

Too much soap leaves a sticky residue that attracts dirt. No-rinse sprays like the Folex leave less. Fabric should feel damp, not soaked, and needs several hours to dry. A final pass with plain water removes leftover soap.

specDecoder.meaning: A tag on upholstery telling you which cleaners are safe: water-based, solvent, either, or vacuum only.
specDecoder.watchFor: Check the code before using any product on this list. If the tag says X, use a vacuum and a dry brush only.

specDecoder.meaning: A suction rating in kilopascals. It has no common standard between brands.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Uwant lists 18 Kpa, so treat it as a rough guide. Run the machine slowly so the suction has time to work.

specDecoder.meaning: Onboard heating that warms water, usually to 120 to 150 degrees F, not a true steam clean.
specDecoder.watchFor: The MUJERBAY states 140 degrees F, while the Bissell uses steam. Hot water can set some stains, so test first.

specDecoder.meaning: A claim that the formula contains few volatile organic compounds. It does not mean it is safe on every fabric.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Folex states it, so still test a hidden spot. Natural fibers like silk need special care regardless of the label.

specDecoder.meaning: Fabric that does not bleed dye when wet.
specDecoder.watchFor: Most sprays here require colorfast fabric. Wet the hidden spot, blot it with a white cloth and check for dye.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fabric safety and codes
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated how each product fits the W, S, WS and X tag system. Water-based sprays and machines suit W and WS fabrics. We noted warnings on velvet, suede and leather. We did not assume any product is safe on every fabric.

howWeEvaluated.title: Machine performance specs
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated heat and suction, including the MUJERBAY's 140 degrees F and the Uwant's 18 Kpa. We treated suction figures as rough. We noted which machines lack a stated heat figure.

howWeEvaluated.title: Tools and capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at included tools, brush heads and tank size. The Shark's four tools and the Uwant's three brush heads stood out. Small tanks scored lower for big sofas. Where a listing gave no tank size, we said so.

howWeEvaluated.title: Residue and care
howWeEvaluated.description: We read the care steps and residue risks from owner feedback patterns. No-rinse sprays scored higher for residue. Machines need rinsing and drying.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value and ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We used each product's relative price tier only to order the field. Maintenance and refills were weighed alongside. All scores are editorial assessments, not measurements. Where a listing was silent on a detail, we said so rather than guessing.

cards.label: Spray
cards.text: The Folex and Carbona act on fresh stains, cost less and need no storage. They cannot extract deep dirt.

cards.label: Machine
cards.text: The Bissell, Shark and Uwant pull dirt out of the cushion. They cost more and need rinsing and drying.

howToChoose.note: Choose a spray for occasional spills and a machine for pets, kids or old stains. If you are unsure, start with a spray and move to a machine if stains return.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A urine eliminator or enzyme, a self-cleaning tool and a pet hair attachment.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Bissell Max Pet and the Uwant both include pet-focused solutions. Both options work best on fresh accidents followed by an enzyme treatment on old ones.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have pets or kids, clean sofas often or need heated extraction. A machine will also handle car seats and stairs, which spreads the cost.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only have an occasional spill, where the Folex or Carbona is enough.

maintenance.why: Residue and moisture cause a sour smell. Rinse both tanks and let them air dry. Empty the dirty tank outdoors if the water is very dark.
Hair and lint clog the nozzle, which is the most common failure. A quick rinse restores suction. Keep a small brush for the screen.
Dyes can bleed and fabrics can water-mark. A test spot saves a cushion.
Fabric should feel damp, not soaked. Fans help and keep mildew away.
Gaskets and hoses wear after years of use. Replace cracked parts early.

faq.q: What do the W and S codes mean?
faq.a: W means water-based cleaners are safe, S means solvent only, WS means either and X means vacuum only. Check the tag before you clean. If the tag is missing, assume water-based products are risky until you test.

faq.q: Can I use a machine on velvet or leather?
faq.a: Avoid it unless the maker's guide allows it. Velvet water-marks and leather can lose its finish. A professional cleaner is the safer option for delicate fabrics.

faq.q: How long does upholstery take to dry?
faq.a: Several hours, depending on the fabric and the machine. Use a fan and keep traffic off. A fan speeds up drying and helps prevent mildew.
Heat helps with grease and set-in stains. For fresh spills, a spray is enough. Cold water works better on blood and milk.

faq.q: Why did my spot leave a ring?
faq.a: Over-wetting or residue causes a ring. Blot, feather the edges and let it dry. A clean damp cloth on the edge of the spot helps blend it.

faq.q: How often should I clean a sofa?
faq.a: Vacuum weekly and deep clean once or twice a year, or sooner after spills. A weekly vacuum prevents dirt from grinding into the weave.
